beats.text: A hospital wants a new appointment system. Before anyone writes code, two questions must be answered.
First: what should the system do? That is analysis. Collect the facts, find the problems, and break the system into its parts.
Second: how will the system do it? That is design. Plan the modules, the screens, the databases, and the interfaces.
Analysis specifies what. Design focuses on how. Always in that order.
Every project has four P's. People: the stakeholders. Product: the software, plus its documents. Project: the activities. And process: the framework that orders those activities.
A project succeeds when the system meets the user needs, is delivered on time, and stays within budget.
Quality means meeting the requirements. A defect is a deviation from the requirements.
And the earlier a defect is found, the less it costs to repair.
Two checks protect quality. Verification asks: are we building the product right? Does the code follow the design? Inspections and reviews are verification.
Validation asks: are we building the right product? Does the system meet the user requirements? Testing is validation.
